description: Deploys a flow as this token: starts it, or restarts it when draftId applies your pending draft of it first (saved as a version the admin did not approve). Without draftId the current version starts (a running flow is a conflict). PiWorker's agent deploy level decides: low allows flows whose risk is at most external and that, compared with the version the admin last approved, do not raise its risk, add no privileged node, change no destination, host, secret reference, risk switch, credentialed request, rate (how often a flow that reaches other services fires), what a global variable receives or what a published tool runs, and add or change no node that reads variables, metadata or what a credential returned; all allows any flow. A refusal says which alert kinds stood in the way. A flow with errors is refused with error.flowIssues, a flow changed meanwhile with conflict. The admin sees every agent deploy and can roll back.

draftId.description: One of your pending drafts of the flow, from pw_save_draft, to apply first.

name: pw_deploy_flow
title: Deploy a flow

description: Runs a flow once in a sandbox and reports each node's input and outputs: one of flow (inline), draftId (one of your drafts) or flowId (a stored flow). Triggers do not start: payload is injected at triggerNodeId. Nodes that are not safe (HTTP, MQTT, e-mail, chat, commands, files, databases, GPIO…) do not run: they are listed in wouldExecute and emit mocks[nodeId] if given. Secrets are empty and variables isolated, so nothing outside PiWorker is reached or changed. A flow with errors does not run (see issues). At most 50 nodes, 10 s, 200 executions; previews are cut to 2 KiB.

draftId.description: One of your drafts (from pw_save_draft); the settings it kept of the stored flow are hidden from the run as with flowId.

flow.description: A whole flow: its nodes and connections. id, state, version, createdAt, updatedAt, tools, totalNodes and totalConnections (as the read views and exported flows show them) are ignored: the flow is named by flowId, or is new.

items.description: A connection from an output port to an input port.

id.description: The connection's id, unique in the flow (letters, digits, '_', '-', '.' or ':'; at most 256).

name.description: The flow's name (at most 256 characters; a draft's at most 100).

items.description: A node. name and risk (as the read views show them) are ignored; inputs and outputs default to the type's ports.

config.description: The node's settings, as its type's config schema describes them. A flow sent inline has no stored values: "<redacted>" is refused (dry-run a stored flow by flowId, or your draft by draftId, to keep its hidden settings). A sensitive setting takes only a {{secret.NAME}} reference. Values a view cut ("…<truncated>", "<truncated>") or partly hid ("<redacted>" inside a value) are refused: they are not the stored values.

configOmitted.description: Must not be true: a view that left this node's settings out cannot be sent back as the node.

id.description: The node's id, unique in the flow (letters, digits, '_', '-', '.' or ':'; at most 128).

position.description: The node's position on the editor's canvas (finite, within ±1,000,000); laid out automatically when absent.

type.description: The node type, from pw_list_node_types (e.g. trigger-interval, action-http).

truncated.description: Must not be true: a view that left nodes, connections or settings out cannot be sent back as the flow.

variables.description: Legacy flow variables (agents may not change them).

flowVars.description: Initial flow variables of the sandbox (at most 64 KiB).

triggerNodeId.description: The enabled trigger (input) node whose output receives payload; may be absent when the flow has exactly one.

description: Lists the node types flows are built from, triggers (input) first, then processing and actions (output): type id, name, risk (safe, external: reaches other services, privileged: acts on the device), ports, settings (type, bounds, default, and the markers sensitive, agentVisible, destination, riskSwitch, operation and rate, present when true) and documentation. A dynamic URL or host, or a risk switch turned on, makes a node privileged. Without arguments the documentation is left out (documentationOmitted): ask for a category or a type to read it; documentation left out to keep a category small comes with the type alone. trigger-tool and action-reply (flow tools) are listed for reference: agents cannot add, change or remove them.

category.description: Only the types of this category, with their documentation: input (triggers), processing or output (actions).

type.description: Only this type, with its whole documentation.

name: pw_list_node_types

description: Saves a draft of a new or changed flow for the admin to review in PiWorker's editor; nothing runs or changes until the admin approves it. A new flow: flow and a name, no flowId. An existing flow: flowId and baseVersion with ops (edits) or a whole flow ("<redacted>" settings keep the current values). Sensitive settings take only {{secret.NAME}} references; flow tools (trigger-tool, action-reply), webhook paths and tokens, risk switches and legacy variables cannot be changed by agents. A draft with errors is refused with error.flowIssues (check it with pw_validate_flow first). The result lists the alerts the admin will see. Follow up with pw_get_draft.

baseVersion.description: The flow's version the change is based on: the version pw_get_flow (or pw_list_flows) showed when you read it. Required with flowId, unless the flow you send carries that version. If the flow changed since, the draft is refused with conflict and error.currentVersion: read it again and redo the change.

flow.description: A whole flow: its nodes and connections. With flowId, version (as the read views show it) is the version the flow was read at: the base when baseVersion is absent, and it must equal baseVersion otherwise. id, state, createdAt, updatedAt, tools, totalNodes and totalConnections (as the read views and exported flows show them) are ignored.

config.description: The node's settings, as its type's config schema describes them. A sensitive setting takes only a {{secret.NAME}} reference. Values a view cut ("…<truncated>", "<truncated>") or partly hid ("<redacted>" inside a value) are refused: they are not the stored values.
